AdapterOut.description:
An enabled adapter for one tenant: whether connection data is stored, and what it can do.

Never the connection data itself (ADR 0033 invariant 8). `capabilities` is null only when
the adapter cannot describe itself.
AdapterOut.title: AdapterOut

AuditEventOut.description: One audit event (ADR 0032): the same columns, in the same order, as an NDJSON line.
AuditEventOut.title: AuditEventOut

CapabilitiesOut.description: What an adapter can do (ADR 0029 `Capabilities`); sets are sorted lists.
CapabilitiesOut.title: CapabilitiesOut

CredentialOut.description:
The state of one credential scope (`adapter_credentials`): names and refs, never a value.

`state` holds the current and previous slot (generation, name, platform ref, delivered flag,
retire time); `outputs` the names of what was delivered to GitHub.
CredentialOut.title: CredentialOut

DeliveryDetailOut.description:
One delivery. `payload` is the stored body parsed as JSON, only for an `operator`.

Never the headers. Null for a `viewer`, after the body was purged (retention) or when the
stored body is not JSON.
DeliveryDetailOut.title: DeliveryDetailOut

DeliveryOut.description: A received webhook delivery (`webhook_deliveries`) without its headers and body.
DeliveryOut.title: DeliveryOut

DeliveryPage.description: A page of deliveries, newest first.
DeliveryPage.title: DeliveryPage

DisableIn.description: The body of `POST /tenants/{t}/disable`: why the tenant is being disabled.

reason.description: Why (1 to 500 printable characters); stored with secret-shaped parts masked
reason.title: Reason

DisableIn.title: DisableIn

GrantOut.description: One role grant of the caller.
GrantOut.title: GrantOut

HostOut.description: A configured GitHub host as the answering replica sees it (ADR 0030).
HostOut.title: HostOut

MeOut.description:
The authenticated caller (`GET /me`).

`tenants` holds at most 200; `tenants_truncated` is true when more exist.
MeOut.title: MeOut

ReconcileOut.description: The answer to `POST /tenants/{t}/reconcile`: the request was recorded (202).
ReconcileOut.title: ReconcileOut

RegistrationOut.description: A stored registration: ids and the secret's reference, never the key or the secret.
RegistrationOut.title: RegistrationOut

RegistrationStartOut.description:
What the BFF renders to start a manifest registration: no secret.

The browser POSTs `manifest_json` (form field `manifest`) to `post_url`; `state` is the signed
one-time value GitHub returns with the `code`, which the BFF forwards to
`POST /hosts/{host}/registration/complete`.
RegistrationStartOut.title: RegistrationStartOut

RepositoryOut.description: A repository the tenant's installation can see (`tenant_repositories`).
RepositoryOut.title: RepositoryOut

RotationOut.description: What a rotation did. Never a credential value.
RotationOut.title: RotationOut

TenantOut.description:
A tenant: one GitHub installation on one host.

`state` is the installation state written by webhook sync; `admin_disabled_at` is the
separate admin-disable column (ADR 0033 "Tenant disable"); `effective_state` combines them:
`disabled` when disabled, otherwise `state`. `admin_disabled_by` (the actor's `sub`) and
`admin_disable_reason` (scrubbed free text) are set with `admin_disabled_at`, else null.
TenantOut.title: TenantOut

TenantRefOut.description: A tenant the caller holds some role on.
TenantRefOut.title: TenantRefOut

WebhookCapabilityOut.description: How a platform's inbound webhooks are authenticated (never a secret).
WebhookCapabilityOut.title: WebhookCapabilityOut

get.description: Audit events of all tenants and the null-tenant events (instance-scoped auditor).
Stream all tenants' audit events as NDJSON (instance-scoped auditor); itself audited.

200.description: One audit event per line (NDJSON), ordered by seq

get.description: One audit event of any tenant, or a null-tenant event (instance-scoped auditor).
Received webhook deliveries, newest first: status, attempts and error, no headers or body.
One delivery. The stored payload (never the headers) is returned only to an `operator`.

post.description:
Make a dead delivery deliverable again (instance `operator`).

Idempotent: a pending delivery is a 200 no-op. A processed one, or one whose body was purged,
is a 409. The change and its `delivery.requeue` event commit together; the answer is the
delivery as `GET` shows it (the stored payload for an operator, never the headers).

get.description: Configured GitHub hosts and their state as the answering replica sees it (instance).

post.description:
Start the GitHub App manifest flow for an unregistered host (instance `operator`).

Returns what the BFF renders: the URL to POST the manifest to, the manifest and a signed
one-time `state` bound to the caller. No secret. A host that already has an App is a 409.

Finish the manifest flow (instance `operator`): the BFF forwards GitHub's `code` and `state`.

The `state` must be the caller's own, unexpired and unused. The code is exchanged server-side,
the PEM goes into the host's signer and the webhook secret into the secret store; the answer
has ids and a reference only. An invalid state or code is a 400.

schema.description: The BFF's forward of GitHub's redirect: the temporary `code` and the returned `state`.
schema.title: CompleteIn

post.description:
Register a hand-made GitHub App (instance `admin`): App id, PEM and webhook secret.

For where the manifest flow is unavailable (GHES enterprise-owned Apps). The key goes straight
into the host's signer; neither it nor the secret is stored in the database, recorded or
returned. A host that already has an App is a 409.

schema.description:
A hand-registered App: its id, its private key (PEM) and its webhook secret.

The key goes straight into the host's signer and the secret into the secret store; neither is
stored in the database, recorded in the audit log or returned.
schema.title: ManualIn

The OpenAPI 3 document of the admin API v1 (any authenticated caller).
The tenants the caller may read, ordered by id.
One tenant; an unknown or ungranted id is a 404.

The enabled adapters: name, whether the tenant has connection data, capabilities.

Never the connection data (ADR 0033 invariant 8): the store is only asked which entries
exist.
One tenant's audit events (an auditor on that tenant, or an instance auditor).
Stream one tenant's audit events as NDJSON; itself audited.

get.description: The tenant's credential scopes: state, names and timestamps, never a value.

post.description:
Rotate a credential scope now (`operator`, instance or on the tenant).

Runs the credential core in this request: a new secret is issued, delivered to GitHub and the
old one retired (two-phase adapters keep it for an overlap and finish later). Calling it again
while a rotation is open resumes that one. No secret value is returned. A disabled tenant, a
scope with nothing rotatable or a busy lease is a 409; a platform or GitHub failure a 502.

Disable a tenant (instance `admin`). Its webhooks are stored but not handled, and no new
adapter operation starts; the installation sync does not change this. Idempotent: a tenant
that is already disabled keeps its first time, actor and reason.
Enable a tenant again (instance `admin`). Idempotent: an enabled tenant is a no-op.

get.description: The tenant's credential operations, newest first.

post.description:
Ask for a reconcile of the tenant soon (`operator`, instance or on the tenant).

Records the request (`ReconcileRequests`, a set, so a repeat is one request) and answers 202;
the reconcile loop that consumes the set is NG5r. A disabled tenant is a 409. The event is
written first, then the request recorded, then the transaction commits: a failure to record
leaves no `success` event.

get.description: The repositories the tenant's installation can see, by numeric id.
The tenant's non-secret adapter resources, by adapter and key.
